Patrick —

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick confirmation below and a proposed run-of-show for access ops: 

Summary answers:
- Pre-authorized badges: yes. We can push QR codes and pre-registration for all redwood attendees and guests listed on the manifest. Please provide full legal names, DOB (for vendor KBA only), and government ID type for contractors — we will not store IDs, only hash and retention metadata per our policy.
- Grayline AV: we require either a) Grayline to provide a vendor insurance & staff list for a light check, or b) Redwood escorts for the demo setup window (recommended if they need network access).
- Devices: corporate laptops with company-managed EDR are permitted in demo zones. Personal devices are allowed only in public reception areas; no unmanaged devices in the secure lab.
- Badge kiosk: Redwood can staff a check-in kiosk in the lobby 07:15–08:30; we will print temporary badges with photo if needed.

Proposed access run-of-show (high level):
07:00 — Redwood onsite security and kiosk setup (Ben & Security Ops)
07:15–08:30 — Badge pickup and verification (pre-registered QR scan or ID check)
08:30–09:00 — Escort to demo lab for guests requiring escorted access
09:00 — Workshop start
16:30 — Demo teardown, Grayline AV declined/unescorted staff must depart by 17:00

Next steps from your side: send final guest list (names/email/company/phone), vendor staff list for Grayline if you want them unescorted, and any SLA/exception requests. Laura — looping you in for any additional controls we should require.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SummitGrid — on-site visitor onboarding and security requests

Marissa / team —

Security checklist and minimal controls we will enforce for the demo area: 

1) Identity verification
- All external vendor staff must present government ID at kiosk for KBA cross-check. If vendor refuses, they must be escorted at all times.

2) Device hygiene
- Only corporate-managed laptops with our approved EDR/MDM profile will be permitted inside the secure demo lab. Personal phones are allowed but must remain on visitor guest VLAN with restricted access.

3) Network segmentation & creds
- No credentials or secret material stored on demo devices. If a vendor must connect equipment to the network, it will land on a segregated VLAN and be blocked from internet egress except to specific IPs we pre-authorize.

4) Physical escorting
- Escorts must be Redwood staff that have completed visitor escort training. Escort list will be provided to SummitGrid so you know who will be with vendor staff.

5) Exceptions & after-hours
- Any after-hours access or SLA exceptions require a signed security-exception-form.docx submitted 48 hours in advance and an on-site badge sponsor.

Please supply vendor staff DOB (for KBA only) and insurance evidence if you want Grayline unescorted. Otherwise we will plan to escort them for setup and teardown.

Laura Bennett
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: security-exception-form.docx

- Complete the security-exception-form only if we need after-hours access for demo teardown.

One last ask — our CISO has asked for an on-site contact for audit questions during the day; can Laura or a designee be reachable at a single number? If so, please provide a contact name and on-site mobile.

Thanks all — looking forward to a smooth day.
